newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES FIRMER IN REDUCED LIQUIDITY.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES FIRMER IN REDUCED LIQUIDITY.

text.p: Zimbabwe's money rates were quoted largely firmer in Tuesday's active market on the back of reduced liquidity.
"The market is a little bit short at the moment...we only have about Z$45 million treasury bills maturing today so we've raised our rates a bit," a dealer said.
"But we're still expecting the treasury bill rate to be lower at this week's tender so everyone is stocking up on treasury bills so they can sell them (for a profit) at a lower rate later," he added.

Discount houses were on Tuesday trading treasury bills at 17.80 percent, up from Monday's 17.70 percent while NCD bills maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were quoted at 19.50 and 18.50 percent (buying and selling) from 19 and 18.75 percent.

Call money added one-and-a-half percentage points to 19 percent but bankers acceptances were quoted stable to easier at 18.50 and 17.80 percent (buying and selling respectively) compared to 18.50 and 18.25 percent.
